def: The run-to-run spread of a score when nothing has changed; the smallest improvement that can be told from no change.
An integer that fixes a program's pseudo-random draws, so that a run can be repeated exactly.
The upward bias in the best of many noisy measurements, which makes a selected result look better than it is.
A comparison that subtracts the two arms seed by seed, removing the luck they share, and tests the differences.
The standard deviation of an estimate such as a mean; it shrinks with the square root of the number of runs.
An exact test that asks how often random sign changes of the observed differences give a mean at least as extreme.
The difference between a change's gain on the proxy score and its gain on held-out data.
Data the research loop never reads, used only to measure whether gains transfer.
The problem that testing many candidates makes some look significant by chance alone.
